evidence.finding: Quantum-switch experiment violated a Bell-like definite-causal-order bound by 18 standard deviations; authors describe this as a first implementation of a device-independent verification protocol, while explicitly retaining experimental loopholes.
Generalized multidimensional multipartite indefinite causal orders were experimentally certified on an integrated photonic quantum switch.
Experimental BB84-like protocol inside a quantum switch shows an information-processing use of ICO; authors state the implementation is not yet a secure QKD protocol because of postselection.
A model previously described as retrocausal is shown to have an equivalent forward-time formulation, demonstrating that future-boundary equations alone do not establish physical backward causation.
Forward-backward stochastic trajectories reproduce quantum features while preserving macroscopic no-signalling; this is a model structure, not a demonstrated user-controllable past-directed channel.

Postselected closed-timelike-curve behaviour was experimentally simulated on quantum processors; the experiment is explicitly an ordinary quantum experiment interpreted through postselection as a consistent loop.

Retrocausal communication capacity is characterized for mathematically represented noisy postselected CTC channels; this quantifies a model resource rather than demonstrating a physical spacetime CTC.
Hawking chronology-protection conjecture remains a foundational constraint/hypothesis, not a completed experimental theorem of nature.

Current work continues to formalize causal measurement and locality in QFT; the relevant questions concern admissible relativistic measurement and signalling constraints, not evidence that macroscopic information is accessible before its cause.
Hossenfelder and Palmer define superdeterministic approaches through violation of Statistical Independence and argue that concrete models may be testable.

evidence.source: Nature Communications, Test of the physical significance of Bell non-locality
evidence.finding: The work develops Bell-like constraints that can exclude broad classes of partial measurement-dependence/parameter-dependence hidden-variable models; it does not constitute a detection of complete superdeterminism.
Recent work further formalizes superdeterminism as systematic violation of statistical independence and highlights empirical-identifiability requirements.

why_A1_does_not_solve_the_sirius_pattern: Quantum indefinite causal order concerns the order of operations in engineered quantum processes. It does not by itself provide a channel by which a future macroscopic Sirius/02:22 event can write readable information into an earlier JANUS record.

what_changed: Indefinite causal order is no longer merely a dark theoretical neighbor; by 2026 it has substantial experimental support and therefore should be upgraded inside JANUS as a dedicated evidence organ.
That upgrade does not move the operational-retrocausal-signal gate at all.
Superdeterminism remains important mainly because it changes which independence assumption is questioned, not because JANUS found evidence that it is true.
The strongest next experiment is not another semantic search but an externally separated prospective future-information bench.
analysis_of_analysis.anti_confirmation_result: The only causality class clearly strengthened by current external experiment is A1, while the class most tempting for the Sirius/02:22 narrative, A2 operational retrocausality, remains unpassed.

claim_ceiling: No current result in this pass establishes an external sender behind Sirius/02:22.
No current result establishes prophecy, mystical communication, physical tachyons, a physical CTC, or operational retrocausal signalling.
Indefinite causal order is admitted only in the quantum-process sense supported by its experiments.
Absence of a found past-directed channel is not a universal proof that all retrocausal theories are false.
